hook: Claude Code can now hand off sessions to your phone or browser
what_it_is: A new /remote-control command bridges a running Claude Code terminal session to claude.ai/code, so you can start work on your laptop and continue or check on it from a browser or phone.
why_you: As a solo builder juggling Short Clips Studio, the kids' games, and Sengoku Campaign between OD consulting gigs, this lets you kick off a build in the morning and check progress or nudge Claude from your phone during a break, without opening a laptop.
prompt_to_try: In Claude Code, run /remote-control on my current Short Clips Studio session and tell me exactly how to open and control it from my phone browser.

hook: A team turned QA into a 'Council' of 8 specialized Claude subagents
what_it_is: OpenObserve built eight role-specific Claude Code subagents that split end-to-end test analysis, generation, and review into stages, each gated by a human check, running as slash commands defined in markdown files.
why_you: This is a concrete, buildable pattern for your QA-for-AI-SDLC thesis: instead of writing about quality leadership in the abstract, you could prototype a small 'council' of 2-3 subagents (e.g. test-planner, test-writer, reviewer) on one of your own repos and turn the experience into your next LinkedIn post.
prompt_to_try: Help me design a mini 'council' of 3 Claude Code subagents (test-planner, test-writer, test-reviewer) for my Hebrew geography game repo, each with a clear role and a human checkpoint between stages, and write the first subagent definition file.

hook: A library of ready-made QA subagents you can drop into any repo
what_it_is: VoltAgent's open-source collection offers over 100 specialized Claude Code subagents, including a dedicated qa-expert agent for test planning, coverage analysis, and quality metrics, packaged as copy-in markdown definitions.
why_you: Rather than writing a QA subagent from scratch, you can pull the qa-expert definition, adapt it to your Sengoku Campaign Godot project or the kids' games, and immediately have a repeatable review step to practice and document for your QA-leadership pivot.
prompt_to_try: Read this QA subagent structure I'm pasting below (from VoltAgent's qa-expert.md), then adapt it into a subagent tailored to reviewing my Godot 4 Sengoku Campaign prototype for bugs, balance issues, and missing edge cases.

hook: Claude Code now shows reasoning effort per subagent, live
what_it_is: The latest Claude Code changelog adds reasoning effort to the subagentStatusLine payload so custom agent rows can render model and effort, plus a periodic progress heartbeat for long-running tool calls that previously went silent.
why_you: You're running role-based agent crews for Short Clips Studio (Strategist, Writer, Producer, Publisher, Analyst) — now you can actually see which subagent is thinking hard vs. coasting, and stop wondering if a stuck-looking long QA or render step has actually died.
prompt_to_try: Set up a status line for my Short Clips Studio agent pipeline in Claude Code that shows which subagent is active and its reasoning effort, then run a full Strategist-to-Publisher pass on one clip idea so I can watch the handoffs.

hook: Opus 4.5's system card added a full web-agent evaluation section
what_it_is: Anthropic's Opus 4.5 system card update added Section 2.22 covering a WebArena evaluation, a structured benchmark for how well an agent completes real, multi-step tasks on live websites.
why_you: This is exactly the kind of scaffolding your QA-for-AI thesis needs — a documented, repeatable rubric for grading agentic task completion, which you could adapt into a lightweight test protocol for your own AI-built apps (trip planners, comic site, kids' games) before you ship them.
prompt_to_try: Read up on WebArena-style agentic evaluations conceptually, then help me draft a 6-step QA checklist I can reuse across my projects — kids' games, trip planners, The Echoes We Leave — that grades whether Claude actually completed multi-step tasks correctly, not just whether the code runs.

hook: Agent Skills can package your QA checklist as a reusable folder
what_it_is: Claude's Skills feature lets you package instructions, scripts, and resources into organized folders that Claude loads dynamically to perform specialized tasks, rather than re-pasting a prompt every time.
why_you: You've been writing a QA-for-AI-SDLC checklist for your LinkedIn series in prose — turning it into an actual Skill means you can drop the same rigor into every project (Sengoku Campaign, kids' games, Short Clips Studio) with one command instead of re-explaining your standards each session.
prompt_to_try: Help me turn my QA-for-AI checklist into a Claude Skill: a folder with instructions for reviewing code changes, flagging untested edge cases, and checking for regressions, that I can invoke by name across my Sengoku Campaign and kids' games repos.
